experiment.yaml:
# ===========================================================================
#  signal-liveness — does the signal ever move?
# ===========================================================================
#  The question the survey says nobody answers. A policy that refuses above 0.90,
#  run where pressure never passed 0.40, reports the same numbers as no policy at
#  all — and a reader cannot tell the two apart.
#
#      admitperf run experiments/signal-liveness --mock              # no GPU
#      admitperf run experiments/signal-liveness --mock --capacity 400  # inert
#
#  WHAT IS DEPLOYED is not described here. It is in the cluster config below,
#  which already declares the model, the engine flags, the topology AND the
#  admission policy. This file says only what load to send and how many times.
#
#  That split is deliberate. The old schema carried its own `infra:` block, so
#  the model was declared in two places and "same cluster, only the load changed"
#  was unverifiable.
# ===========================================================================
name: signal-liveness

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  CLUSTER — what we are sending load at
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Everything about the deployment comes from here, including which admission
#  policy is active and at what threshold:
#
#      admission:
#        policy: kv_threshold        <- resolved from src/admitperf/policies/
#        params: {threshold: 0.90}
#
#  To test a different policy, point at a cluster config that declares it. To
#  test the same policy under a different topology, point at pair.yaml or
#  disagg.yaml. The experiment does not change either way.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
cluster: infra/config/single.yaml

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  LOAD — what we send
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  kind      poisson | fixed. Poisson because real arrivals are bursty, and a
#            fixed rate understates queueing
#  n         total requests
#  rate      arrivals per second, OFFERED. Whether the cluster serves them is
#            the thing being measured
#  seed      fixed, so two runs face the same trace. Without it, a difference
#            between policies may be a difference between traces
#  tokens    prompt and output length. These decide how long a request lives,
#            and therefore concurrency: concurrency = rate x duration. Short
#            requests cannot fill a cache no matter the arrival rate
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
load:
  kind: poisson
  n: 90
  rate: 12
  seed: 0
  prompt_tokens: 2048

  # Long enough that requests OVERLAP, which is the whole point. Concurrency is
  # rate x duration, so short requests cannot fill a cache at any arrival rate.
  # Against the mock a request lives 0.05 + output_tokens x 0.01 seconds, so 120
  # tokens is ~1.25 s and 12 arrivals/s gives ~15 concurrent — past a capacity-8
  # engine. At 24 tokens it would be ~3 concurrent and the run comes back INERT.
  output_tokens: 120

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  BASELINE — what the policy is measured against
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  The same load with admission disabled. Without it, "the policy admitted 82%"
#  has nothing to be 82% of, and any latency figure is uninterpretable.
#
#  Run as a separate arm against the SAME cluster, so the only difference is
#  whether the policy was consulted.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
baseline: no_admission

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  REPEATS — the error bar
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  One run has none, so a gap between two policies may be noise. Three is the
#  minimum that gives a spread; reporting item 4 fails below it.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
repeats: 3

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  EXPECTED — written before the run, checked after
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#  Recorded here so the prediction cannot be edited to match the result. The
#  report compares against it.
#
#  On single.yaml: 7B bf16 on one A100-40 leaves ~22 GB of KV, so ~12 concurrent
#  at 32k. A 2048-token request at 256 output tokens lives long enough that 15
#  arrivals/s should push past 12 concurrent and fill the cache.
#
#  If the signal stays flat, the run is INERT and the fix is the LOAD, not the
#  policy: longer requests or a higher rate. That diagnosis is the whole point of
#  reporting liveness.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
expect:
  signal: kv_used_fraction
  reaches_threshold: true
  limiter: kv

cluster.yaml:
# ===========================================================================
#  single — 1 GPU, aggregated
# ===========================================================================
#  Start here. The fewest things that can be wrong.
#
#      python -m infra.render infra/config/single.yaml --plan
#
#  What this proves        the bring-up works, the gateway reaches a worker,
#                         decisions are logged, a report is produced
#  What it cannot show     placement. One worker means one destination, which
#                         is routing rather than a decision
#  Admission IS real       ~12 concurrent sequences at 32k, and KV binds before
#                         max_num_seqs, so a KV policy can fire
# ===========================================================================
extends: base.yaml

topology:
  mode: aggregated
  # Each engine does prefill and decode for its own requests, so no KV hop
  # exists and kv_transport must not be set.
  pools:
    engine:
      replicas: 1
      tensor_parallel_size: 1
      host: gpu-1
